requirements.statement: Every active accepted requirement SHALL have exactly one canonical Assurance correspondence declaring applicability required or none.
A required Assurance obligation SHALL be resolvable through the governed issue or PR audit context and the applicable structured semantic-audit receipt for the exact subject.
FS0 Assurance SHALL support requirement-quality, ambiguity, contradiction, Design-fidelity, Plan-fidelity, Build-fidelity, Conformance-interpretation, and evidence-sufficiency review.
An adverse semantic-audit receipt SHALL block the applicable merge or issue closure until a later satisfactory receipt applies to the same exact subject.
Every Assurance audit receipt SHALL make governed work, exact subject, required obligations, outcome, evidence, material exclusions, and audit time resolvable.
A review subject SHALL NOT authorize its own Assurance review.
An Assurance audit conclusion SHALL be specific to the exact governed audit subject identified by its applicable structured receipt.
Each installed Assurance correspondence record SHALL contain requirement_id, applicability, and obligation_ids.
In the fixed FS0 GitHub binding, maintained Assurance provenance SHALL use governed issue and pull-request state/history rather than duplicate repository-tree case or finding artifacts.
An Assurance audit receipt or conclusion SHALL NOT independently create, amend, supersede, or withdraw persistent normative authority.
Persistent semantic change identified by Assurance SHALL route through Governance Design.
An Assurance correspondence with applicability required SHALL contain at least one stable review-obligation identity.
An Assurance correspondence with applicability none SHALL contain an empty obligation_ids collection.
Candidate and completion semantic-audit receipts, GitHub evidence/history, and their merge or issue-closure dispositions SHALL be remotely accessible.
Assurance requirement-quality review SHALL detect materially compound identified requirements and material semantic omission caused by statement-length compression.
